name: Pronouns
description: Personal, possessive, reflexive, interrogative, and demonstrative pronouns by case.

items.prompt: {0} komme morgen um neun.
items.translation: I am coming tomorrow at nine.
items.explanation: 1st-person singular subject is *ich*.

items.prompt: Wann kommst {0} nach Hause?
items.explanation: Informal 2nd-person singular subject is *du*.

items.prompt: Mein Bruder ist Lehrer. {0} arbeitet in Berlin.
items.translation: My brother is a teacher. He works in Berlin.
items.explanation: 3rd-person masculine singular subject is *er* (referring to a male person or a masculine noun).

items.prompt: Meine Schwester ist Ärztin. {0} wohnt in München.
items.translation: My sister is a doctor. She lives in Munich.
items.explanation: 3rd-person feminine singular subject is *sie* (referring to a female person or a feminine noun); capitalised here at the start of the sentence.

items.prompt: {0} fahren am Wochenende ans Meer.
items.translation: We are going to the sea on the weekend.
items.explanation: 1st-person plural subject is *wir*.

items.prompt: Die Kinder spielen draussen. ___ haben viel Spass.
items.explanation: 3rd-person plural subject is *sie* (lowercase; not to be confused with formal *Sie*).

items.prompt: Kannst du {0} morgen anrufen?
items.explanation: 1st-person singular accusative is *mich* (direct object of *anrufen*).

items.prompt: Ich verstehe {0} nicht ganz.
items.explanation: Informal 2nd-person singular accusative is *dich* (direct object).

items.prompt: Da ist Peter. Siehst du {0}?
items.translation: There is Peter. Do you see him?
items.explanation: 3rd-person masculine accusative is *ihn* (direct object referring to a male person or masculine noun).

items.prompt: Anna ist meine Freundin. Ich besuche ___ am Samstag.
items.explanation: 3rd-person feminine accusative is *sie* — same form as the nominative, distinguished by context.

items.prompt: Der Lehrer fragt {0} oft auf Deutsch.
items.translation: The teacher often asks us in German.
items.explanation: 1st-person plural accusative is *uns* (same form serves the dative).

items.prompt: Eure Eltern haben angerufen. Sie suchen {0}.
items.translation: Your parents called. They are looking for you all.
items.explanation: Informal 2nd-person plural accusative is *euch* (same form serves the dative).

items.prompt: Kannst du {0} bitte helfen?
items.explanation: 1st-person singular dative is *mir* — *helfen* governs the dative.

items.prompt: Ich gebe {0} morgen das Buch zurück.
items.translation: I'll give you back the book tomorrow.
items.explanation: Informal 2nd-person singular dative is *dir* (indirect object of *geben*).

items.prompt: Tom hat Geburtstag. Wir schenken {0} ein Buch.
items.translation: Tom has a birthday. We're giving him a book.
items.explanation: 3rd-person masculine dative is *ihm* (indirect object of *schenken*).

items.prompt: Maria ist krank. Wie geht es {0}?
items.translation: Maria is sick. How is she doing?
items.explanation: 3rd-person feminine dative is *ihr* (here with the dative idiom *wie geht es …*).

items.prompt: Die Kollegen brauchen Hilfe. Ich helfe ___ gleich.
items.explanation: 3rd-person plural dative is *ihnen* (lowercase; the formal *Ihnen* is capitalised). *Helfen* takes the dative.

items.prompt: Herr Schmidt, kann ich {0} etwas anbieten?
items.translation: Mr Schmidt, can I offer you something?
items.explanation: Formal *Sie* in the dative is *Ihnen*, capitalised.

items.prompt: Ich wasche ___ die Hände.
items.explanation: Reflexive 1st-person singular accusative is *mich* (same form as the personal accusative).

items.prompt: Setz ___ bitte hin!
items.explanation: Reflexive informal 2nd-person singular accusative is *dich* (same form as the personal accusative).

items.prompt: Er freut ___ auf den Urlaub.
items.explanation: All 3rd-person reflexives — singular and plural, all cases — collapse to *sich*.

items.prompt: Die Gäste unterhalten ___ gut.
items.explanation: All 3rd-person reflexives — singular and plural, all cases — collapse to *sich*.

items.prompt: Wir treffen ___ um sieben am Bahnhof.
items.explanation: Reflexive 1st-person plural is *uns* in both accusative and dative — identical to the personal pronoun.

items.prompt: Beeilt ___, sonst kommt ihr zu spät!
items.explanation: Reflexive informal 2nd-person plural is *euch* in both accusative and dative — identical to the personal pronoun.

items.prompt: ___ kommt heute Abend zur Party?
items.explanation: *Wer* asks about the subject (nominative): who?

items.prompt: ___ hast du gestern auf der Strasse getroffen?
items.explanation: *Wen* is the accusative interrogative: whom (direct object)?

items.prompt: Mit ___ sprichst du gerade am Telefon?
items.explanation: *Wem* is the dative interrogative: to/for whom? *Mit* governs the dative.

items.prompt: ___ Auto steht da vor dem Haus?
items.explanation: *Wessen* is the genitive interrogative: whose?

items.prompt: ___ machst du heute Nachmittag?
items.explanation: *Was* asks about a thing: what? Used for both subject and direct object.

items.prompt: ___ Mantel hier gehört mir.
items.explanation: Demonstrative *dieser* before a masculine nominative noun — same *-er* ending as the definite article *der*.

items.prompt: ___ Tasche ist sehr teuer.
items.explanation: Demonstrative *diese* before a feminine nominative noun — same *-e* ending as the definite article *die*.

items.prompt: Ich nehme ___ Kuchen, bitte.
items.explanation: Demonstrative *diesen* before a masculine accusative noun — same *-en* ending as *den*.

items.prompt: Mit ___ Schlüssel öffnest du die Tür.
items.explanation: Demonstrative *diesem* before a masculine dative noun — same *-em* ending as *dem*. *Mit* governs the dative.

items.prompt: Das ist ___ Schwester aus Hamburg.
items.explanation: Possessive *mein* (my) gains *-e* before a feminine nominative noun (*meine Schwester*).

items.prompt: Hast du ___ Schlüssel gesehen? Ich finde ihn nicht.
items.explanation: Possessive *mein* (my) gains *-en* before a masculine accusative noun (*meinen Schlüssel*).

items.prompt: Sie spricht oft mit ___ Bruder am Telefon.
items.explanation: Possessive *ihr* (her) gains *-em* before a masculine dative noun (*ihrem Bruder*). *Mit* governs the dative.

items.prompt: Er hilft ___ Mutter im Garten.
items.explanation: Possessive *sein* (his) gains *-er* before a feminine dative noun (*seiner Mutter*). *Helfen* governs the dative.

items.prompt: Wie heisst ___ Tochter eigentlich?
items.explanation: Possessive *euer* (your, informal plural) drops the second *e* and gains *-e* before a feminine nominative noun (*eure Tochter*).
